instruction: Three-Operation Machining of a Casting `scene.blend` contains a single mesh object `Casting`: a rectangular blank aligned to the world axes with X extent `[-1, +1]`, Y extent `[-0.7, +0.7]`, and Z extent `[0, 1.0]`. On this machine, the Blender executable is `/opt/blender/blender`; use it to open `scene.blend`. Machine it into the final part below and save the result as `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend`. Requirements: 1. Keep exactly one mesh object, still named `Casting`. 2. Leave the object's world location and rotation unchanged. Do not apply Object transforms (no `Object > Apply > Location/Rotation/Scale` and no equivalent `bpy.ops.object.transform_apply`); keep `obj.location` equal to the input value `(0, 0, 0.5)` and `obj.rotation_euler` equal to `(0, 0, 0)`. 3. Save a final mesh with an empty modifier stack. 4. The final mesh must be closed and manifold, with no loose geometry. 5. Face off the top by `0.1 BU`, so the top face lies at `Z = 0.9` while the X and Y extents stay unchanged. 6. Add a central vertical through-hole of diameter `0.5 BU` on the world Z axis, passing from `Z = 0` to `Z = 0.9`. 7. Add two blind pin holes of diameter `0.1 BU` with axes parallel to world X, centered at `(Y, Z) = (0, 0.45)`, one entering from `+X` and one from `-X`. Each blind hole is `0.45 BU` deep, so the flat blind ends lie at `X = +0.55` and `X = -0.55`.
